statement: At period end, owners and bookkeepers need to hand their external accountant or tax preparer a complete set of books (GL detail, trial balance, aging, bank recs) in a shape the accountant can use, without hours of manual reassembly.
notes: Near neighbour of p-02 (audit-trail export for compliance) and p-17 (continuous GL sync). Key signal: a periodic handoff of the books themselves, not change history and not an ongoing integration. Often phrased as a file format (CSV, XLSX, IIF, Xero file).

statement: Finance and compliance teams at audited or regulated companies need a tamper-evident history of who created, changed, approved or deleted financial records, which they can produce for auditors.
notes: Easily confused with p-01 because requests say 'export for our auditors'. The need is change history and accountability (who/when/old/new), not the ledger. Also brushes p-12 when the trigger is a sensitive field being changed.

statement: Managers need to review and approve employees' expense claims before they are reimbursed, with routing based on amount, category or team.
notes: Near neighbour of p-04 (vendor bill approvals). Distinguish by what is being approved: employee out-of-pocket spend and reimbursement vs supplier invoices in AP. Words like 'expenses' appear in both (property 'maintenance expenses' are bills).

statement: AP teams need vendor bills checked and approved by the responsible budget owner before they are scheduled for payment, so nothing is paid that shouldn't be.
notes: Near neighbour of p-03. Vendor/supplier/contractor/subcontractor invoices, segregation of duties between entering and paying. Not employee reimbursements.

statement: Businesses selling internationally need to invoice and get paid in their customers' currencies and see what they actually received in their home currency, including FX differences.
notes: Near neighbour of p-06. This is a single legal entity billing in foreign currency. Currency translation of a foreign subsidiary for group reporting belongs to p-06. EU VAT reverse charge belongs to p-14.

statement: Groups with several legal entities need consolidated financial statements across entities, with intercompany activity eliminated, without stitching spreadsheets together.
notes: Near neighbour of p-05 (mentions currencies when subsidiaries are abroad) and p-12 (entity-level access). Signal: several entities/LLCs/subsidiaries rolled up into one view.

statement: Bookkeepers spend hours manually matching bank transactions to invoices and bills, especially when one deposit covers many invoices, amounts arrive net of fees, or references are unclear.
notes: Hot problem. Near neighbour of p-08 (feed missing data) and p-19 (recording partial payments). Here the transactions are present but matching them is slow or fails.

statement: Bank connections silently stop syncing or sync incompletely, so transactions go missing and users don't notice until balances are wrong.
notes: Near neighbour of p-07: users often describe it as 'can't reconcile'. Signal: transactions absent, duplicated after reconnect, or connection broken without warning.

statement: Businesses get paid late and waste time chasing overdue invoices because follow-up with customers is manual and inconsistent.
notes: Near neighbour of p-10 (making it easy to pay) and p-15 (overdue invoices on a cash dashboard). Signal: follow-up/chasing/reminders/statements after the invoice is sent.

statement: Customers want to pay an invoice immediately by card or bank transfer from the invoice itself, and the business wants that payment recorded automatically.
notes: Near neighbour of p-09. Some requests mention reminders but the real blocker is that paying is inconvenient (checks, wires).

statement: IT teams at larger customers need Ledgerly sign-in and user lifecycle managed centrally through their identity provider, including MFA policy and instant deprovisioning.
notes: Near neighbour of p-12: both are 'access'. This is authentication and account lifecycle, not what a signed-in user can see or do.

statement: Admins need to control which users can see or change which data (by entity, department or sensitive area like payroll or vendor bank details), beyond the fixed Admin/Finance/Viewer roles.
notes: Near neighbour of p-11 (an IT admin asking for 'access control' may mean either) and p-20 (accountant access across clients).

statement: Businesses that bill the same customers on a fixed schedule need those invoices created and sent automatically instead of rebuilding them every period.
notes: Often requested as a 'duplicate invoice' button. Distinct from p-09: the invoice is never sent late because nobody remembered to create it, not because the customer didn't pay.

statement: Businesses selling across states or countries need the correct sales tax or VAT applied to invoices and reported, without looking up rates and rules by hand.
notes: Small but strategically sensitive. EU VAT requests can look like p-05 (international invoicing).

statement: Owners and finance leads need to see their upcoming cash position from what is due in and due out, so cash shortfalls don't take them by surprise.
notes: Can be confused with p-09 when phrased as 'overdue invoices dashboard'. Signal: forward-looking cash position combining receivables and payables.

statement: Businesses need invoices that carry their branding and the fields their customers require (PO numbers, project codes, terms) so invoices are accepted and paid without reissuing.
notes: Mostly solution-shaped (logo, custom fields). Enterprise variant is about customer AP rejecting invoices missing PO numbers.

statement: Companies that keep their general ledger in QuickBooks, Xero or NetSuite need Ledgerly transactions to flow there continuously and correctly, without duplicates or re-keying.
notes: Near neighbour of p-01. Signal: an ongoing integration that misbehaves (duplicates, missing refunds, latency) vs a one-off handoff file. Accountants submit both.

statement: Expense evidence gets lost between purchase and month end; employees need to capture receipts at the moment they spend so finance doesn't have to chase them.
notes: Can be confused with p-03 when the symptom is 'approvals stuck because receipts are missing'.

statement: Businesses need to record deposits, partial payments, progress billing and credits against invoices so the balance a customer owes is always correct.
notes: Near neighbour of p-07: a partial payment that 'won't reconcile' is really about recording it against the invoice.

statement: External accountants and bookkeeping firms need to work across all of their clients' Ledgerly accounts from a single login, with the right access in each.
notes: Long tail but strategically important (partner channel). Near neighbour of p-01 (accountant needs the books) and p-12 (access).
